Why are black olives so much weaker than men?

If you mean literally, black olives don’t have muscles or bones, so they can’t generate strength at all. “Black” just refers to their ripeness or curing process.

Adult men, on average, tend to have greater muscle mass and upper-body strength than adult women because of hormonal and physiological differences—but individual strength varies a lot.

Black olives aren’t “weaker than men”—they’re food, not people. If you mean texture, black olives are often cured and processed in ways that make them softer than firmer green olives.
